spec.title: PROP-072: Source interpretation and boot observability

p.SOURCE-DESCRIPTOR-GRAMMAR: A package may declare sources in repeated `[[package.sources]]` TOML tables. Each row has exactly one selector, `file = "package-relative/path"` or `directory = "package-relative/path"`; `directory` is a default for descendants, not a glob, and neither selector may escape the package root or name a generated output. Each row requires `media`, `interpretation`, `role` and `loading` strings. The initial interpretation vocabulary is `vibe-spec`, `vibe-doc`, `commonmark`, `xml-data`, `opaque`; the role vocabulary is `spec`, `documentation`, `resource`; the loading vocabulary is `scan`, `explicit`. `scan` may enumerate a declared source of any interpretation, but only `vibe-spec` or `vibe-doc` may mint their respective Vibe facts or addresses. Ordinary CommonMark contributes structural navigation without Vibe facts; XML data and opaque resources remain data or raw bytes. `media` records the declared media type separately from interpretation; it must be a normalized nonempty media-type token and is checked against the selected reader before that reader runs. An unknown value or incompatible combination refuses rather than widening a parser. The descriptor's durable resource identity is the package coordinate plus its normalized relative file path, independent of filename suffix, target materialization format and current physical bytes. No table field grants trust: origin, selected declaration, captured source bytes, source hash, generated/authored status and verification are host-observed provenance, retained separately from authored intent.

p.SOURCE-DESCRIPTOR-PRECEDENCE: For one normalized file identity, an exact `file` row wins over every matching `directory` default. Otherwise the longest matching directory path wins; a directory matches only its own descendant components, not a textual prefix. Identical equally specific declarations may coalesce, but incompatible equally specific rows produce a path-specific `NeedsInput` outcome and confer no semantics. A selected declaration must still pass media/syntax validation. Extension, location, parsable XML, Markdown markers and successful syntax sniffing never create a missing Vibe declaration. A source with no proved interpretation remains raw and unclassified; a foreign bridge source defaults to no Vibe interpretation. In a `simple` package, literal `#use` and related directive-looking text remain literal package content; descriptor selection does not change the package-format and boot-link contracts.

p.SOURCE-HOST-OPT-IN: A plain `[project]` may opt into the same descriptor row grammar and precedence with repeated `[[project.sources]]`; an absent or empty list preserves its legacy source behavior until that consumer is migrated. The host resource identity is its validated self coordinate (`group/name`) plus the normalized project-relative path. A declaration grants no trust or Vibe fact: a semantic consumer first captures source bytes under the project root, selects the row, checks media and reader compatibility, and retains its own witness. A project without a valid self coordinate cannot mint `spec://` addresses from these rows. Ordinary CommonMark, XML-data and opaque sources remain literal resources; merely naming one under the specs root never enrolls it as a Vibe document or boot directive. A consumer that cannot prove a cited row, its bytes or a complete directory census refuses before changing adoption state.

p.SOURCE-EXPORT-SELECTOR: An ordinary CommonMark section becomes a durable navigation export only through a repeated `[[package.source_exports]]` row with a package-unique ASCII `name` token (`[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._-]*`), one normalized exact `file` path and a nonempty ordered `headings` array of exact normalized heading titles from the document root to the selected section. The file must select a `commonmark` descriptor with `text/markdown` media before parsing; an export row does not itself grant interpretation, trust or a Vibe fact. The host captures the source bytes once and resolves each heading segment among the direct child sections of its selected parent. A missing segment, malformed selector, ambiguous sibling title or changed source witness refuses; no first-match or ordinal fallback exists. The durable export identity is the package coordinate plus export name, while the resolved node ID is local to one parsed snapshot. A successful observation retains that snapshot's source hash and byte span so later use must recheck the same captured source rather than treating the authored row as physical proof. Directive-looking CommonMark text and inline code remain literal; no export mints a Vibe fact or directive.

p.SOURCE-REPRESENTATION-COLLISION: A source's normalized package-relative path is its declared resource identity; a materialized output path and a Vibe document address are separate identities with separately captured mapping evidence. Before conversion, derive selects the descriptor on the original source path. Only a selected Vibe spec/document interpretation may enter the Vibe parser or change serialization; `commonmark`, `xml-data` and `opaque` keep their exact raw bytes and do not become Vibe documents because of `.md` or `.xml`. A same-stem ordinary Markdown file and XML-data file are independent resources and may coexist. Two selected Vibe representations claiming one document address, or two resources requiring the same output path under the target's filename-equivalence policy, refuse before publication; no extension-order preference or silent overwrite exists. A resolver may pair Vibe forms only from a validated source-to-output map carrying interpretation and source witness, not from stem alone. Legacy undeclared package paths retain their explicitly bounded compatibility route until the source-consumer migration owns their replacement. Case and Unicode filename equivalence differ across hosts: compare aliases that can be proved statically, use no-replace publication and refuse collisions actually observed on the target, and warn when host alias equivalence remains unproved. A missing cross-platform proof does not by itself ban unrelated Unicode paths or make Linux unusable.

p.SOURCE-MIGRATION-LAW: Source declaration migration extends the incumbent M-13 authored-manifest planner, exact replay, one-file application admission and recovery journal; it does not create another executor. Its source and target profiles, recipe and recognized old grammar are explicit, finite and revisioned. No package version, absent manifest epoch, suffix, directory convention or syntactically valid content selects a source interpretation. An old authoritative declaration may be translated only when its meaning maps uniquely; conflicting or unknown per-resource intent yields a typed, path-specific `NeedsInput` question and leaves the authored file unchanged. A successful plan retains exact before/after text, ordered edits and identities; insertion of new declaration rows is represented by validated zero-length edits, and multiple edits replay in source order. All untouched bytes, including comments, whitespace, quote style, existing field values and order, survive exactly. The current Manifest owner validates the complete result after the frozen profile check. If the edit span, question, profile or output cannot be proved, migration refuses; planning never writes, and application still requires the existing explicit ownership grant and recheck.

p.SOURCE-OBSERVATION-LAW: Every interpreted read, projection, conversion, scan and refusal identifies the normalized resource; it carries the selected descriptor and declaration origin when one exists, the captured byte identity when bytes were read, the reader/converter recipe when one ran, and whether positions refer to source or projection. A missing descriptor, unsupported media or vocabulary, ambiguous selection, invalid syntax and unavailable bytes remain distinct incomplete or unsupported observations; none is reported as an empty document or successful scan. Ordinary data remain retrievable as original bytes even when optional structure inspection fails. This contract extends PROP-045 `SOURCE-CLASSIFICATION-LAW`; it does not assert that existing scanners, resolvers, materializers, boot readers or migration surfaces already implement it.

p.CAPTURED-GRAPH: VibeVM projects existing compiler IR, observer evidence and committed boot summaries without replacing their semantics. Logical sources, ordered contributions and repeated occurrences remain distinct. Every available inclusion edge, requested address and position retains its captured meaning. Missing occurrence-to-edge or source-position mappings are explicit gaps, never guessed paths. Projection retains the complete existing typed compiler carrier alongside its graph view, including lane chunks, absorption/link plans and emitted witnesses. Dynamic-index entries retain order, multiplicity, kind and unevaluated conditions; the static pointer remains distinct from entries. Whole-run inspection traverses one captured index and reports each snapshot outcome without hiding unavailable children.

p.IDENTITY: Retained inspection preserves the exact run, scope, event sequence, invocation and snapshot filename. Summary captures carry caller-supplied identity and are not compiler snapshots. Graph traversal retains every captured child and occurrence; source deduplication must not deduplicate occurrences.

p.KNOWLEDGE: Unknown means not checked. Unresolved requires a checked negative result. A retained snapshot that was never recorded is unavailable; one named but absent is missing, with eviction claimed only from evidence. Unreadable or invalid data is an explicit refusal.

p.READ-ONLY: Retained reads never open a trace writer, invoke a provider, run retention or silently compile replacement data. Existing compiler wire validation and trace index validation remain authoritative. Zap owns planning and acceptance; PodBay owns physical process execution.

p.CAPTURED-MEASUREMENT: Measurements retain capture identity, source byte witnesses and a revisioned recipe. Raw and emitted bytes, Unicode scalar counts, unique payload and ordered repeated occurrences are separate quantities from the same captured graph. Direct and inclusive attribution require recorded mappings; missing mappings remain unavailable, never zero or proportional allocation. INDEX declarations and unevaluated conditions do not prove runtime reads. Token counts name tokenizer identity, version and recipe with exact, estimated or unavailable status; no ratio is exact tokenization. Unobserved ambient context remains unknown separately. Inspection is read-only and does not compile, hydrate, install, call a provider or claim provider billing. Chunked traversal imposes no total boot-size or token admission threshold. Tree JSON and install/update closure diff carry the same typed calculation; before captures precede apply and are never reconstructed afterwards. Existing scalar observer samples and default unavailable observation behavior remain compatible.

p.DEBUGGER-CAPTURE-POLICY: Trusted boot and prepared-source capture has no fixed resource or aggregate diagnostic size admission ceiling. Bounded editor buffers and transport requests retain their independent limits. Finite disk capture retains owned immutable bytes with held no-follow, single-link, two-pass equality and final-name identity proofs; observed file length fences coherence, not boot admission. Overflow, allocation and I/O failures remain explicit failures. Retained capture memory may scale with content; bounded transport does not prove constant heap. This adds policy separation without replacing any captured graph, read-only, identity, measurement or hypothetical law.

p.DEBUGGER-SCALE-EVIDENCE: Scale evidence names its fixture recipe, generated byte and scalar quantities, ordered occurrences and unique versus repeated payloads. Synthetic whitespace units are not model tokens. Total result size, actual page or chunk frame maxima, transport working storage and process memory observations are separate quantities; a viewport or bounded reader alone proves no bound on retained capture or total debugger heap. Cancellation evidence identifies the inspection terminal outcome and preserves the independent compiler outcome. Missing tokenizer, memory or capture evidence remains explicitly unavailable. High-size capture refusal cannot serve as proof of scalable inspection. This evidence clause extends CAPTURED-MEASUREMENT without replacing CAPTURED-GRAPH, READ-ONLY, DEBUGGER-PROTOCOL, the viewer and hypothetical laws, or PROP-048 BOOT-NO-ADMISSION-QUOTAS.

p.DEBUGGER-PROTOCOL: The shared debugger route registers strict epoch-bound inspect, tree, explain, cost, compare, capture and inspection-only cancel requests and result/error/progress carriers. CLI structured input and MCP delegate to one host-bound route retaining immutable M16 captures, original-byte position basis and snapshot/result identities. Page sessions retain exact context, capture and filter; stale, replayed or foreign cursors refuse. Stream replay uses the incumbent event model and reports gaps explicitly. Cancelling inspection never requests or claims build cancellation. Captured costs retain the incumbent measurement recipe, unavailable tokenizer/billing/ambient-tail facts and no boot admission quota. Reads never invoke compilation, providers, retention, installation or model activation. Host-granted capture and overlay authority remain separate from transport values. Finite captures are not atomic all-files observations, source authentication or hostile-writer proofs.

p.DEBUGGER-CAPTURED-JOINS: Snapshot comparison uses active captured resource presence, not the declaration inventory. A successful finite capture proves bytes or absence; unavailable reads refuse capture rather than becoming absence. Creation and deletion are added and removed; changed requires bytes on both sides. Graph source indices resolve through their retained identity catalogue and are not host resource indices. Available emitted-artifact spans retain one-based inclusive line meaning and exact snapshot, artifact resource and digest. Absent spans and unproved authored-resource joins remain explicit null values; emitted lines never become authored XML coordinates. The registered compiler carrier remains available with its original format identity when captured, preserving source trees and positions without reconstruction.

p.DEBUGGER-VIEWER: The D-007 standalone inspector is a thin local presentation over the shared debugger route, available as `vibe boot --view` with line-oriented interactive commands and a headless script surface. It presents captured occurrences, source catalogue, inclusion explanations, original-byte chunks and exact two-snapshot comparison with explicit diagnostics. It introduces no IDE extension or D-025 plugin MVP. The existing package-tree TUI remains governed independently by PROP-037.

p.DEBUGGER-VIEWER-IDENTITY: Selection, viewport and navigation are presentation state only. Row ordinals resolve to captured contribution/occurrence pairs; labels and paths never become semantic IDs. Snapshot selectors resolve only to exact IDs returned by the current host. Domain queries use typed shared service requests and retain context, immutable snapshot, source witness and refusal semantics. Refresh explicitly captures a new observation; it never replaces a selected old snapshot silently. Comparison reports the shared service's resource differences and both snapshots' gaps without inventing graph-edit or authored-source evidence.

p.DEBUGGER-VIEWER-PARTIAL: Large captured graphs support bounded visible windows and ordinal, parent and child navigation without recursive traversal or a boot-size admission quota. Missing source, parent and authored-position mappings remain explicit unavailable observations. Source reads use captured resource IDs and bounded original-byte chunks, never opening displayed paths. Interactive viewer registration owns its terminal with a typed Interactive classification distinct from structured stdin's PersistentProtocol. Headless frames retain the same typed nodes, provenance and differences as the API; presentation escaping cannot change their identities. Reads preserve canonical boot artifacts and never acquire overlay, compiler or provider authority.

hypothetical.title: 8. Frozen hypothetical world and pure builtin preview

p.HYPOTHETICAL-SCENARIOS: Explicit scenario controls construct immutable add, remove, toggle and reconfigure candidate requests from a named retained baseline. Add and remove change declared root intent; toggle records an explicit enabled or disabled selection; reconfigure records the requested feature, configuration or continuity branch without choosing a missing mandatory alternative. The original baseline, request, choices and source captures remain available and unapplied. The package-source owner normalizes candidate intent through the incumbent resolver and captures both complete selected worlds; adapters and the viewer do not solve dependencies, substitute installed state or sum independent package deltas. A branch change preserves unrelated shared contributions through complete-world comparison, retaining package membership, features, effective dependency edges, declaration/provider provenance and qualified cost evidence. Every scenario binds the requested OS target and legal loading intent. Unevaluated conditions remain potential contributions, never exact future runtime reads or total session cost. Missing mandatory selection and illegal static/dynamic placement produce typed incompatibility; missing content or unsupported preparation produces a named incomplete result. An ordinary CLI or registered MCP route may expose an explicitly admitted local capture producer, separately from pure retained evaluation; no transport request grants fetch, install, hydration, native execution or publication authority. Viewer and machine clients use the same captured draft, selectors and comparison model, so repeating evaluation over those retained inputs reproduces the same result. This extends HYPOTHETICAL-BINDING, HYPOTHETICAL-CAPTURE, HYPOTHETICAL-AUTHORITY, HYPOTHETICAL-STAGES, HYPOTHETICAL-NO-WRITES and MARGINAL-COMPARISON independently; it does not assert that scenario production is implemented.

p.HYPOTHETICAL-BINDING: The package-source composition may explicitly bind a prepared scenario into the existing debugger host route. Its baseline and candidate host inventories are retained immutable document captures; its selected package rows, effective edges, choices and catalog witness come from the same admitted InstallResolver transaction used for installation. Explicit local source capture checks the catalog identity before and after reading; unavailable remote bytes require a named fetch/source stage. The shared preview request names the prepared scenario and expected baseline, candidate and catalog identities, never a caller-authored graph or a path to open. Evaluation checks those expected witnesses against the retained binding; it does not discover whether live files have changed. Newly captured catalog or source inputs have new world identities and cannot satisfy an older expected witness. Finite capture does not claim atomic observation against a hostile writer. Host configuration is distinct from transport: ordinary CLI/MCP inspection does not acquire a prepared scenario automatically. Missing descriptor derivation, conditional-resolution projection, effective subskills, hybrid units or owner-runtime evidence stays an explicit incomplete stage; no simplified replacement semantics may claim completion for those inputs. A dynamic-only lane has placements and no compiled static artifact; missing measurements remain absent or unavailable.

p.HYPOTHETICAL-CAPTURE: An explicit hypothetical computation binds the baseline and candidate source captures, the exact captured catalog witness, admitted choices, target conditions and expected world identity before evaluation. Candidate resolution uses the incumbent normalized request and frozen transaction catalog authority; a preview must not introduce another solver or reconstruct captures from current installed state. Source bytes, manifests and selected package identities belong to the same prepared scenario. Missing captures remain named incomplete inputs. A changed expected catalog, source capture or world identity refuses as stale rather than silently rebinding the scenario.

p.HYPOTHETICAL-AUTHORITY: Legal static and dynamic placements retain the incumbent loading, ordering, owner and condition semantics. A requested loading override that the package contract does not permit is incompatible; evaluation never edits the package to make the request legal. Supported pure builtin compilation uses the existing compiler with captured source inputs, entirely in memory. Its graph preserves the compiler carrier and the captured graph laws; its metrics use the same qualified measurement recipe. Repeating an identical prepared scenario produces identical hypothetical graph and metrics, including explicit unavailable measurements.

p.HYPOTHETICAL-STAGES: The shared debugger request/result protocol distinguishes explicit hypothetical computation from captured inspection. Results retain the bound scenario identity and distinguish a completed supported builtin preview, incompatible intent and incomplete preparation with the exact missing stage or capture. An unavailable native compiler, uncaptured source or required fetch is a named incomplete stage; preview never invokes a native backend, fetch, installation or publication implicitly. Effectful admission and preparation require their separate explicit authority and are not supplied by a hypothetical request.

p.PREVIEW-PREPARATION: Preparation is a separate explicit command over a host-registered immutable plan: context, captured input, ordered stage, exact selected source/content witness and noncanonical cache destination are presented before execution. Transport cannot mint a capability. A host-issued preview capability uses the incumbent SubmissionReservations, SubmissionJournal and LifecycleLease on the preview cache; Install and Deploy authority do not authorize preview preparation. Only a new durable reservation can invoke a provider. Complete and partial outcomes retain each valid stage's captured bytes before proceeding; a later failure retains those bytes and its typed stage outcome. Interrupted or uncertain publication requires recovery and never reruns a provider. Inspecting retained preparation evidence opens only existing pinned read state, without admission, leases or a live provider, including after provider revocation. The first supported producer is exact local-registry fetch through the incumbent catalog-checked fetcher into a separate preview cache. Remote fetch, embedded/composed hydration and native compilation without an installed scoped producer remain named unavailable stages; no generic support is inferred from a provider interface. Preparation leaves installed project manifest, lock, slots and canonical boot unchanged. Cache/journal writes are effects even if the selected source was already local. These laws extend HYPOTHETICAL-STAGES and preserve all independent capture, graph, measurement and no-write laws.

p.HYPOTHETICAL-NO-WRITES: Pure hypothetical evaluation leaves project manifests, lockfiles, dependency slots and canonical boot artifacts unchanged. READ-ONLY, CAPTURED-MEASUREMENT and DEBUGGER-PROTOCOL continue to govern ordinary inspection: inspect, tree, explain, cost, compare and viewer reads do not compile or prepare a scenario. Hypothetical computation does not replace current-world observations or promote candidate state. These clauses specify required behavior; they do not assert that a production preview route or prepared-input constructor is already implemented.

p.MARGINAL-COMPARISON: Pure comparison evaluates both complete frozen worlds with the incumbent captured builtin compiler. Each result retains both world, catalog, host capture, admitted request, selected choice, technical declaration/provider and effective configuration witnesses, selected package membership, source byte hashes, compiler contribution and ordered occurrence identities. Marginal cost is checked signed candidate-minus-baseline for the same qualified recipe and lane, never a sum of independent experiments. Package raw direct cost counts its selected boot declarations; raw inclusive cost counts the set of reachable selected packages once, including shared and transitive dependencies. These source quantities are distinct from compiler emitted direct/inclusive mappings and whole-artifact framing. Repeated compiler occurrences remain repeated even when dependency membership is shared. Independent experiment deltas are non-additive and cannot be aggregated without a new complete joint world. Static emitted artifact, static raw declarations and dynamic potential raw declarations remain separate; dynamic payloads and conditions do not prove runtime reads or session cost. Missing transitive, configured, conditional, owner or native capture remains named unavailable, never successful zero. A partial result retains both worlds and any available lane evidence. This extends, and does not replace, CAPTURED-GRAPH, CAPTURED-MEASUREMENT and all HYPOTHETICAL laws.

p.DEBUGGER-SURFACE-PARITY: Equivalent retained inspect, source chunk, explain, cost and compare requests use the same immutable capture and typed service results across library, canonical API, structured CLI, registered MCP and viewer. The viewer exposes full inspection, including resource inventory and compiler carrier, alongside its occurrence viewport; any captured resource may be read by resource ordinal in bounded original-byte chunks, including selected projections with their distinct coordinate basis. Cost retains its qualified recipe and unavailable diagnostics unchanged. Equal payload bytes never authorize merging source, owner, base, local, result or occurrence identities. Unsupported native inverse mappings remain unknown; retained inspection cannot execute a removed provider. This clause adds surface reachability without replacing any independent graph, measurement, hypothetical, derivative, authority or read-only law.

p.DEBUGGER-DERIVATIVE-HISTORY: Explicit host composition may retain a checked derivative-result catalogue with one immutable capture. Structured inspection carries that catalogue as an optional JSON array of strict derivative-result records. It preserves exact base/local/result inventories and observed identity independently of live source or provider availability. It does not create compiler provenance: without captured owner evidence joining an actual contribution and occurrence to a bound result, that join stays unavailable. Repeated occurrences keep the incumbent contribution/occurrence identities even when a retained payload identity is shared. Retention never mutates an existing snapshot, opens a trace writer, invokes a provider or computes a replacement derivative. This additive clause preserves all graph, measurement, read-only, viewer and completeness laws and does not assert ordinary host configuration is wired automatically.

p.DEBUGGER-DERIVATIVE-PRODUCER: Explicit scenario preparation may produce a protected same-invocation derivative capture: successful compiler worklist reads plus its actual strict closure and emitted bytes. The ordinary local producer accepts only checked selected Vibe-spec descriptor inventories; unsupported descriptors, bridge and owner-runtime preparation remain explicitly incomplete. Inspecting the retained produced snapshot exposes exact result/base/local records and independent raw and selected-projection resource identities. Repeated occurrences retain distinct compiler ordinals while sharing the same source/result. Raw authored resources use original_bytes; generated selected text uses captured_projection, never native raw coordinates. A viewer may select the produced snapshot after explicit preparation, then navigate retained source bytes. No inspect, tree, source or chunk request recompiles or rebinds that snapshot. Legacy artifact captures without this producer evidence remain unavailable for such joins. Current-base authentication, absent parent-edge evidence and other captured gaps remain explicit.
